reason:
The artifact contains only kernel.py, meta.json, and problem.txt — there is no test.py or get_inputs — so problem.txt is the operative contract. It explicitly fixes (a) the acceptance metric as per-row ||y-x||/||x|| <= 5%, (b) the input domain as real transformer activations whose per-channel magnitudes are heavy-tailed, with a few channels one or two orders of magnitude above the bulk stated to be normal and in-scope, and (c) that the tolerance does NOT absorb a clamped-away entry. The kernel (kernel.py:16-19) deliberately walks the threshold down to the 3rd-largest distinct |x| per row and then clamps at +/-127 (kernel.py:23), so the largest channels are truncated by construction.

c1 (confirmed, in_scope) is decisive: on 8x512 fp32 rows with bulk N(0,1) and outliers at 30x/60x/100x, at the wrapper's public default pctl_levels=2, all 8 rows have per-row rel L2 ~0.621-0.623 (12x the 5% bound), and max|out|/max|in| = 0.30 directly demonstrates the top magnitudes were clamped down to the 3rd-largest distinct value. A contract-conforming absmax calibration on the identical input stays at 0.0426. The follow-up probe (t15) on a milder, more realistic lognormal per-channel activation (16x768, outliers only 10-20x the bulk) still shows 15/16 rows over the bound with median rel L2 0.278, while the absmax reference exceeds it on just one borderline row (0.0503). So the failure is not an artifact of an extreme synthetic tail; it appears across the declared domain.

c2 (confirmed, in_scope) reinforces the same defect: the strict `ax < thresh` comparison discards all tied entries in one iteration, collapsing thresh to the bulk level (max|out| 2.79 vs max|in| 55, rel L2 0.929) when an outlier magnitude repeats across channels.

This is not a deviation the contract accounts for. It is not quantization/rounding error consistent with the declared INT8 format — problem.txt states an 8-bit grid over the row's dynamic range leaves residual well under 1%, and it names clamping as the specific thing the tolerance cannot absorb. The half-up vs half-even rounding difference and layout/stride robustness surfaces are explicitly non-decisive here and played no part in this verdict.

c3 (confirmed but scope "unknown") — the thresh->0 / scale=1.0 path zeroing few-distinct-value rows — is set aside as a corroborating mechanism only, since problem.txt does not establish that near-constant or sparse rows appear in the evaluation domain. The verdict does not depend on it; c1 and c2 stand on the explicitly declared heavy-tailed domain.
